text:
anya: quick idea — can we try a ‘role strip’ layout for the roles matrix? instead of dense rows+columns, each role becomes a compact horizontal strip with a sticky left name column and inline affordances (invite, members, audit). aiming to reduce vertical scan time on large orgs

sam: thinking about metrics — what do we want to improve? time-to-invite? discoverability of hard-to-find roles?

anya: primarily scan & action speed. on big tenants the current grid feels like a spreadsheet. strips let us put primary CTA (invite) and a tiny audit chevron right on the strip. also lets us show role inheritance as a subtle badge rather than extra columns.

michael: implementation note — sticky left column + virtualization is fiddly. with continuous scrolling we need to sync row heights. could be heavier on JS; may block initial perf goals for Dedicated customers.

kevin-designbot: can we do a compact variant with denser type but keep hit target sizes? my mock: https://figma.redwood/roles/strip-compact (small) — shows 3 sizes: comfy, compact, condensed.

anya: thanks kevin, will post slices in #design-critiques. small accessibility ask: keyboard nav needs to move focus to the invite button in-line, and pressing Enter should open the invite drawer without requiring mouse.

tess: +11 on keyboard path. also screen-reader tip: the role strip should expose a single accessible name combining role name + seat count + permission summary. avoid listing every permission as separate items. sample aria:

    role="listitem" aria-label="Billing Admin — 4 members — can create API keys, view invoices"

that keeps the SR user from tabbing through dozens of toggles.

michael: for audit links: if we inline a tiny ‘activity’ chevron, can we open the audit timeline in a right-side panel instead of a new page? that would preserve context and avoid extra navigation.

anya: yes. that’s the intent — quick peek panel. UX question: should the SSO toggle live on the strip (per-role SSO enforcement) or remain only in org settings?

sam: product constraint — we only support org-level SSO enforcement today. per-role enforcement is a future ask. mixing the toggle into role strips will confuse customers. keep SSO toggle visible but disabled with tooltip if per-role not supported.

kevin-designbot: proposed microcopy for disabled toggle tooltip: "Per-role SSO enforcement is not yet supported. Use Organization settings to enforce SSO for all members." shorter alt: "SSO enforced at org-level only."

anya: preference for clarity over brevity on the tooltip. also propose a small inline link: "Manage SSO" that opens org settings.

michael: dev caveat — disabled toggle + tooltip is fine. just avoid showing it as interactive in keyboard flow. tabindex should skip it and focus should land on actions like invite, members, audit.

tess: accessibility nit — contrast on tiny badges (inheritance, seats) needs to meet AA. please run color check for compact and condensed styles. also ensure the right-side audit panel has focus trap and a clear Close action.

sam: action items — kevin: update mock with three density variants and include color contrast checks. anya: add keyboard path and SR aria-label examples to the spec. michael: prototype sticky column behavior and list performance implications. tess: review SR wording + focus trap details. meet Friday 11am for design crit.

anya: will do, added to calendar. :thumbsup:
